blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Strategic decisions are rarely made with clean data. Most of the time, the executive is choosing between imperfect options, on the basis of partial information, while the environment continues to change underneath them. The honest response is not to pretend otherwise, but to make better decisions despite the fog.

There are a few tools that help. One is to separate the quality of the decision from the quality of the outcome. A well-reasoned decision can still end badly, and a reckless one can still end well; confusing the two systematically erodes the judgement of any leadership team. Another is to build explicit plans for being wrong — what would we do differently, how quickly would we notice, what would it cost to reverse?

Perhaps most importantly, mature decision-makers cultivate the habit of distinguishing three very different things: what the data shows, what they believe on the basis of experience, and what they are frankly guessing. Each of those has its place in a decision, but conflating them quietly is how boards end up confident about things they should be cautious about.

items.q: According to the text, what is the honest response to imperfect information?
options: To delegate the decision to a specialist
To pretend the uncertainty is not there
To postpone the decision until the data is clean
To make better decisions despite the fog
items.why: "The honest response is not to pretend otherwise, but to make better decisions despite the fog."

items.q: Why does the text warn against confusing the quality of a decision with the quality of the outcome?
options: It makes decisions slower
It systematically erodes the judgement of a leadership team
It increases the cost of reversing a decision
It removes accountability from the board
items.why: "confusing the two systematically erodes the judgement of any leadership team."

items.q: What three things do mature decision-makers distinguish?
options: Cost, timing and risk
Strategy, structure and incentives
Evidence, consensus and precedent
What the data shows, what they believe, and what they are guessing
items.why: "what the data shows, what they believe on the basis of experience, and what they are frankly guessing."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A well-reasoned decision guarantees a good outcome.
Blending belief and evidence can create false confidence.
Partial information is the normal condition of strategic choice.
Leaders should plan for the possibility of being wrong.
items.why: Inferência: o texto afirma que uma decisão bem fundamentada pode acabar mal — logo, não garante bom resultado.

items.q: The phrase "conflating them quietly" suggests that the danger is greatest when…
options: the confusion goes unnoticed and unexamined
the confusion happens openly and is debated
the board lacks any data at all
experience is valued over evidence
items.why: Inferência: "quietly" implica que o problema é a mistura passar despercebida, não ser discutida abertamente.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie conduzindo a revisão estratégica. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, before anyone asks — yes, I know the board wants a decision by Friday, and yes, I am going to insist we run a proper pre-mortem first. It will cost us ninety minutes. It will save us a great deal more than that.

Here is how I want us to do it. Imagine it is a year from now and this decision has gone badly wrong. Do not tell me it might fail — assume it has failed, spectacularly, and then work backwards. What did we miss? What were we quietly guessing while telling ourselves it was analysis?

I am particularly worried about reversibility. If we can unwind this in a quarter for very little cost, then frankly we should move fast and stop agonising. But if this locks in eighteen months of capital, the bar has to be far higher, and I would rather be slow than sorry.

One last thing. When you bring me your view, label your confidence. Tell me whether it rests on evidence, on experience, or on a hunch. All three are welcome in this room — but I want to know which is which before we commit.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Sophie insist on doing before the final decision?
options: Gathering more market data
Delaying the board deadline by a week
Running a proper pre-mortem
Bringing in an outside consultant
items.why: "I am going to insist we run a proper pre-mortem first."

items.q: How does Sophie want the team to frame the pre-mortem?
options: By voting on the most likely outcome
By assuming the decision has already failed and working backwards
By listing every possible risk in order
By comparing it with a past project
items.why: "assume it has failed, spectacularly, and then work backwards."

items.q: Why does Sophie treat reversibility as decisive?
options: Because it is the cheapest option to measure
Because it removes the need for a pre-mortem
Because irreversible commitments justify a much higher bar before acting
Because the board asked her to focus on it
items.why: "if this locks in eighteen months of capital, the bar has to be far higher."

items.q: When Sophie says "What were we quietly guessing while telling ourselves it was analysis?", she implies that…
options: analysis is always superior to intuition
the team has done no analysis at all
guesses can be disguised as rigorous analysis
the board should not be trusted
items.why: Inferência: ela alerta que palpites podem se mascarar de análise — daí a necessidade de expô-los.

items.q: What does Sophie's request to "label your confidence" reveal about her leadership style?
options: She values epistemic honesty over false certainty
She prefers consensus to individual judgement
She rejects intuition and wants only hard data
She is uncomfortable making any decision
items.why: Inferência: ela aceita evidência, experiência e palpite — mas exige que se distinga cada um, valorizando a honestidade epistêmica.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "She refused to conflate what the data showed with what she hoped was true." To conflate means to…
options: merge two distinct things as if they were one
exaggerate deliberately
restate more simply
quietly ignore
items.why: To conflate = misturar/confundir duas coisas distintas como se fossem uma só.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Because the deal could be unwound cheaply, its high ___ made her comfortable moving fast."
options: judgement
reversibility
bias
sunk cost
items.why: Reversibility = reversibilidade: se dá para desfazer barato, pode-se agir com mais rapidez.

items.q: Epistemic humility is best described as…
options: modesty about the limits of what one actually knows
avoiding responsibility for outcomes
deferring to the most senior person in the room
a reluctance to make any decision
items.why: Humildade epistêmica = precisão sobre o que de fato se sabe (e o que não se sabe) — não é indecisão.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "We had already spent two million, but she reminded us that a ___ should not drive a future decision."
options: sunk cost
second-order effect
pre-mortem
bias
items.why: Sunk cost = custo afundado: o já gasto e irrecuperável não deve pesar nas decisões futuras.

items.q: "Good second-order thinking asks: and then what?" This describes…
options: reconsidering the decision a second time
seeking a second opinion
ranking options in order of cost
tracing the consequences of the consequences
items.why: Pensamento de segunda ordem = pensar nos efeitos dos efeitos, não só na primeira consequência.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em decisões estratégicas sob incerteza. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's weigh up the options before committing capital." To weigh up means to…
options: carefully assess and compare
postpone indefinitely
measure the cost only
reject outright
items.why: Weigh up = ponderar, avaliar e comparar as opções com cuidado.

items.q: "If it goes wrong, how quickly can we back out of the commitment?" To back out of means to…
options: double down on it
renegotiate its price
announce it publicly
withdraw from it
items.why: Back out of = recuar, desistir de um compromisso já assumido.

items.q: "We can't keep throwing good money after bad on this project." This means…
options: investing more to justify past losses
cutting the budget too aggressively
delaying every payment
spending on a rival project instead
items.why: Throwing good money after bad = insistir em gastar por causa do já perdido — a armadilha do sunk cost.

items.q: "Before we decide, let's stress-test the assumptions." To stress-test means to…
options: simplify them for the board
check how they hold up under adverse conditions
keep them confidential
approve them quickly
items.why: Stress-test = submeter premissas a cenários adversos para ver se resistem.

items.q: "She wanted to keep our options open until the picture cleared." This means to…
options: share every option with competitors
preserve the freedom to choose later
commit to one path early
abandon the decision entirely
items.why: Keep our options open = preservar a opcionalidade, evitar se comprometer cedo demais.
